t: A small county in the Swabian Jura, ruled from Zollern castle and Hechingen by the Swabian branch of the Zollern dynasty.
Its Franconian cousins became Burgraves of Nuremberg and later rulers of Brandenburg, Prussia and Germany.
The Catholic counts rose through Habsburg service, gaining Haigerloch and Sigmaringen before dividing the county in 1576.
dyk: The present Hohenzollern Castle is the third on its hilltop: the medieval fortress was razed by the Swabian imperial cities in 1423, and its successor was rebuilt in the 1850s–1860s.
ev: The counts of Zollern are first mentioned in a chronicle
The sons of Burgrave Frederick I divide the Franconian and Swabian lands
The Schalksburg line sells its lands to Württemberg
The Swabian imperial cities take and raze Zollern castle
Rebuilding of Zollern castle begins under Jos Niklas I
Eitel Friedrich II acquires the lordship of Haigerloch
Charles I receives Sigmaringen and Veringen as Austrian fiefs
The county is divided into Hechingen, Sigmaringen and Haigerloch

f.founder: Count Frederick of Zollern, son of Burgrave Frederick I of Nuremberg
